content:
Apple TV 剛為訂閱用戶新增了一批經典電影，此舉於秋季一輪電影陣容特別強勁前夕推出。

Apple TV 於秋季重磅片單登場前率先加入新片。

Movies are all the rage right now. With box office hits like Blossom Apple, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and Obsession helping drive cultural enthusiasm, the movie industry appears to be thriving.

Apple seems to be looking to capitalize on that as well.

This week, Apple TV added a large catalog of classic films for subscribers to watch for free. The titles vary slightly by region, but in the US, there are acclaimed options like The Martian, Arrival, Eye in the Sky, The Big Sick, MEMORIES OF MURDER, and 21 Jump Street, among others.

With these new additions, Apple nearly doubled its catalog overnight.

However, just because Apple purchased the rights to these movies doesn't mean it's abandoning its own original films. In fact, this sudden influx of new titles comes just before a packed fall lineup of new movie releases.

Here are six new movies coming to Apple TV this fall:

  • September 4: Mayday
  • October 2: The Last First: Winter K2
  • October 9: Matchbox The Movie
  • October 16: Tenzing
  • November 13: Being Heumann
  • November 25: Way of the Warrior Kid

Apple has always walked a line between Oscar bait and crowd-pleasing popcorn flicks. This fall, it looks like there's a fairly even split between the two.

Mayday, Matchbox, and Way of the Warrior Kid all look like lighthearted action-comedies starring stars like Ryan Reynolds and John Cena, while Being Heumann, Tenzing, and The Last First are clearly aiming for awards.

Apple continues to find success on the TV side of things with recent returns like Ted Lasso. It'll be interesting to see how the company's film ambitions play out.

Apple TV costs $12.99 per month, or you can bundle it with other services through Apple One for a discount.
